gloss: dead leaves; dry leaves; fallen leaves

definitions.gloss: dead leaves; dry leaves; fallen leaves
definitions.explanation: Leaves that have dried up and fallen from trees or plants, especially in autumn and winter. A common seasonal image in literature and everyday language.

examples.japanese: {枯|か}れ{葉|は}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{舞|ま}っている→舞う：04573_mau⟧。
examples.english: Dead leaves are swirling in the air.

examples.japanese: ⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{枯|か}れ{葉|は}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦{落|お}ちていた→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧。
examples.english: There were lots of dead leaves on the road.

examples.japanese: ⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{枯|か}れ{葉|は}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}めて→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧⟦{焚|た}き{火|び}→焚き火：06992_takibi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I gathered the dead leaves in the yard and made a bonfire.

notes:
An evocative seasonal word strongly associated with late autumn and winter. In Japanese poetry and literature, {枯|か}れ{葉|は} conveys transience, loneliness, and the passing of time. In everyday use, it simply refers to dried, fallen leaves.

FORMS:
{枯|か}れ (withered, dried) + ⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧ (leaf)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {枯|か}れ{葉|は}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{舞|ま}う→舞う：04573_mau⟧: dead leaves dance in the wind
- {枯|か}れ{葉|は}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{踏|ふ}む→踏む：01197_fumu⟧: to step on dry leaves
- {枯|か}れ{葉|は}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}める→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧: to gather fallen leaves
- {枯|か}れ{葉|は}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧: a pile of dead leaves

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{落|お}ち{葉|ば}→落ち葉：14108_ochiba⟧: fallen leaves — emphasizes the act of having fallen; broader and includes fresh leaves that have just dropped
- ⟦{紅葉|もみじ}→紅葉：05387_momiji⟧: autumn leaves — focuses on colorful leaves still on trees or freshly fallen, with a positive aesthetic nuance
- ⟦{落葉|らくよう}→落葉：17301_rakuyou⟧: leaf fall, defoliation — more formal/botanical term for the process of leaves falling
